I am a 58-year-old farmer in Mtwara, and this 0.43-hectare plot is my cashew stand. Chemical fertilizer and pesticides are too expensive for me to buy from the shop in town, and the voucher program never seems to reach our village, so I will depend on the manure I collect from my goats and cattle to give the trees some strength. This plot has been in the family for years with the same local cashew trees, and we rely on the rains that come — I have no means to irrigate. My wife and children will help with weeding and harvesting, but the plot is small enough that we can manage the work ourselves without hiring anyone from the village.
